text:
ryan: Quick Q — I'm adding a TF change to create a k8s ServiceAccount with IRSA annotation in the `inference` namespace. Plan is to attach an IAM role and bind a namespaced Role for k8s permissions. Snippet I'm planning:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "inference_sa" {
  metadata {
    name      = "inference-worker"
    namespace = kubernetes_namespace.inference.metadata[0].name
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.irsa_inference.arn
    }
  }
}
```
Is that sufficient? Any RBAC gotchas?

lia: Two quick things: 1) Make sure the cluster has an OIDC provider configured and the IAM role trust policy uses the exact subject `system:serviceaccount:inference:inference-worker`. 2) TF may try to recreate the SA if you change the annotation later — that can cause pods to restart. If you need to patch annotation after creation, do it carefully (kubectl patch or use a k8s provider lifecycle strategy).

jess: Also: use a Role (namespaced) + RoleBinding not ClusterRole unless you truly need cluster-wide perms. Keep least privilege. For example Role that allows reading ConfigMaps + listing pods in that namespace: 
```yaml
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: inference-read
  namespace: inference
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps", "pods"]
  verbs: ["get", "list"]
```
RoleBinding subject should be the SA: 
```yaml
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: inference-worker
  namespace: inference
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: inference-read
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

dmitri: FYI: IAM trust policy example (condensed) — you must use issuer host and exact sub claim: 
```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/id/ABCDE12345" },
  "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
  "Condition": {
    "StringEquals": {
      "oidc.eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/id/ABCDE12345:sub": "system:serviceaccount:inference:inference-worker"
    }
  }
}
```

lia: Small TF tips: 1) Use `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` annotation (exact key). 2) If you manage SA + annotations in TF, ensure you use the same namespace resource and `kubernetes_namespace.inference` exists before SA. You can add an explicit `depends_on = [kubernetes_namespace.inference]` on the SA resource to avoid ordering issues.

ryan: Good call. One more: pods that already exist will keep the old projected token; do we need to rollout deployments to pick up the new IRSA role?

jess: Yes, you need to restart pods (deployment rollout). IRSA uses projected serviceaccount tokens mounted into pods at mount time; new token with new audience/claims only appears for new pods. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name> -n inference`

infra-bot: deploy-bot: terraform plan (staging) finished — no diffs for current infra branch :white_check_mark:

dmitri: Also watch for the case where you accidentally create a ClusterRoleBinding to a ServiceAccount — that grants cluster-wide perms. Prefer a RoleBinding in `inference`.

lia: To validate after apply: 
- `kubectl get sa inference-worker -n inference -o yaml` (check annotations)
- `kubectl describe rolebinding inference-read-binding -n inference`
- `kubectl exec -n inference <pod> -- curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (just to sanity-check network, but IRSA uses tokens, not IMDS)

ryan: PTAL @jess @dmitri — I've pushed the TF branch `infra/irsa-inference-sa`. Main things left: add OIDC provider check, add Role + RoleBinding, add depends_on for namespace, and update README. Can someone review? :eyes:

jess: I'll take it. Quick sanity check: ensure role ARN interpolation in annotation -> `aws_iam_role.irsa_inference.arn` and not `.id` or other field. Also check for typos in the annotation key.

dmitri: I can review IAM policy / trust. If you want, add the trust JSON into a gist and drop link here.

ryan: Thanks — I'll add the trust policy gist and request review. Planning to roll this out to staging first, then prod after validation.

lia: One more operational note: add a small tilt/liveness check that fails pod if it can't assume the role (so we detect IAM miss configs early) — optional but helpful.

ryan: Great, will do. Thanks everyone :rocket:
